details: Primitive Subsistence: Small patches, family labor, simple tools (hoe, dao), slash-and-burn (Jhumming).
Intensive Subsistence: High population pressure on land, high chemical inputs and irrigation to maximize yield.
Commercial Farming: Large land holdings, high HYV seeds, synthetic fertilizers, mechanization for market export.
evidence_or_examples: Jhumming in North-Eastern states; Rice cultivation in Punjab as commercial crop vs Odisha as subsistence.

details: Kharif: Sown June-July (monsoon onset), harvested Sept-Oct (Paddy, Maize, Jowar, Bajra, Cotton, Jute).
Rabi: Sown Oct-Dec (winter onset), harvested April-June (Wheat, Barley, Gram, Mustard).
Zaid: Short summer season between March-June (Watermelon, Muskmelon, Cucumber, Fodder crops).
evidence_or_examples: Paddy in monsoon belts; Wheat production in western Himalayan winter precipitation belts.

branches.theme: Major Food, Cash, and Non-Food Crops

details: Rice: Staple food, hot & humid climate (>25°C), high rainfall (>100 cm), clayey alluvial soil (WB, UP, Punjab).
Wheat: Cool growing season (10-15°C), bright sunshine ripening (21-26°C), 50-75 cm rainfall (Punjab, Haryana, UP).
Millets: Jowar, Bajra, Ragi (rich in iron/calcium, drought resilient).
Sugarcane: Tropical/subtropical crop, 21-27°C, 75-100 cm rainfall (UP, Maharashtra).
Tea & Coffee: Plantation beverage crops; Tea in Assam/WB; Coffee (Arabica variety) in Baba Budan Hills, Karnataka.
Rubber & Fiber Crops: Rubber in Kerala (>200 cm rain); Cotton (black Regur soil, 210 frost-free days); Jute (golden fiber, Hugli basin).
evidence_or_examples: Kerala leading in natural rubber; Maharashtra leading in cotton; West Bengal leading in jute.

details: Land Reforms: Land consolidation (Chakbandi), abolition of Zamindari system.
Green Revolution & White Revolution (Operation Flood): Modern HYV technological inputs.
Institutional Protection: Kisan Credit Card (KCC), Personal Accident Insurance Scheme (PAIS), Minimum Support Price (MSP).
Bhoodan-Gramdan Movement: Initiated by Vinoba Bhave ('Bloodless Revolution') for voluntary land redistribution.
evidence_or_examples: Shri Ram Chandra Reddy offering 80 acres in Pochampally; MSP announcements protecting farmers from market drops.
